messages:
margot: heads up — customers started hitting indexer rejects after last night's schema migration and the large backfill kicked off. errors show VectorDB rejecting batch with \"expected vector dim 1536, got 1024\". noticed this after ~10% of backfill rows failed.

ian_supp: ugh. which model did the embeddings service start returning? any chance we swapped to a different embed model in the release?

margot: not that I can see in the deploy notes. infra deploy was only schema migration to v2 (field change + stricter vec length check). backfill tool still points at /v1/embeddings in the job config.

chen_ml: logs from the embeddings service show the model id header as \"open-embed-1024-q\" for some requests and \"open-embed-1536\" for others. looks like traffic split during canary. maybe the canary used a quantized 1024-d variant.

margot: here's the actual error payload from the indexer: ```json
{"time":"2026-06-11T02:12:45Z","job":"indexing","batch_id":3421,"error":"vector_dim_mismatch","expected":1536,"got":1024,"sample_id":"cust_9921"}
```

miguel_ops: ops-bot just recorded a deploy around 02:05 UTC: `deploy service=embedder tag=2026-06-11-canary-embed split=10%`. ops didn't think it impacted indexer because indexer doesn't call embedder directly — backfill fetches embeddings via API.

elena_product: flagged high-priority for impacted enterprise customer (acct: org-ferris). they saw 12k failed rows and dropped ingestion. billing spike concers too if we re-run naive.

ian_supp: immediate mitigation: pause backfill, revert embedder canary or pin backfill to the stable model. we should not accept 1024-length vectors into the vecdb.

chen_ml: quick repro steps I used: ```bash
# request current default embeddings model
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \\
  -d '{"input":"test","model":"default-embed"}' \\
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings | jq .
# sample python snippet
from requests import post
r=post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings', json={"input":"foo","model":"default-embed"}, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer ..."})
print(r.json())
``` saw `model: open-embed-1024-q` in 1/10 responses when sending 100 requests.

margot: job config for backfill: ```yaml
job_name: v2_indexer_backfill
embeddings_endpoint: https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
model: default-embed
batch_size: 128
workers: 8
``` so it uses whatever default mapping gives.

miguel_ops: rolled back the canary at 02:30 UTC. ops-bot: `deploy rollback service=embedder to=2026-06-09-stable`. verifying embedder now returns 1536 consistently.

chen_ml: after rollback, ran a quick 200-request smoke and saw all embeddings length 1536. still, we have ~30k failed rows from the window. we need a plan: either re-embed those rows with the stable model or mark them for special handling.

ian_supp: plan proposal: 1) identify failed batch ids from indexer logs (we have list) 2) pause customer-facing re-ingest until scheduling window 3) create a targeted backfill that forces model: open-embed-1536 (explicit model id) and smaller batch_size 32 to reduce memory/timeout errors 4) validate dims before upsert and write a dry-run to the staging index 5) run billing-safe re-ingest with progress checkpoints (SUP-1423)

elena_product: customer ok with pause as long as we give ETA and avoid duplicate charges. please ensure we track which rows were retried.

margot: notes on root cause: the default model routing changed in a canary deploy (model alias resolution returned a quantized 1024-d variant). Indexer assumed the backend embedding dimensionality is constant and the schema migration added a strict check that now rejects mismatch. two fixes: make indexer tolerant (not ideal) or ensure model aliasing doesn't change dims without a controlled churn.

chen_ml: created quick PR to make backfill CLI accept an explicit `--model-id` flag and a preflight dimension check (https://git.internal/redwood/embeddings/pull/812). keeps backfill from accidentally using alias.

miguel_ops: scheduling targeted backfill for 2026-06-11 04:30 UTC with lower concurrency. ops will watch token usage. reminder: reduce concurrency to limit billing impact.

vector-bot: alert: target re-ingest job v2_indexer_backfill_retry started at 2026-06-11T04:31:12Z job_id=rb-20260611-01 expected_rows=30234

ian_supp: checklist for retry run: - explicit model-id set - batch_size 32 - preflight embed dimension check (fail fast) - write progress markers to s3 - dry-run option to validate first 500 rows - notify customer before final commit

margot: after first 1k rows dry-run: 0 mismatches. good. will proceed with full retry.

elena_product: customer notified (they appreciate the update).

margot: final status: retry finished 2026-06-11T07:10Z. all previously failed rows successfully indexed with 1536-d embeddings. created follow-up doc summarizing incident, mitigation steps, and product change to add model-dim invariants to rollout playbook. ticket SUP-1423 remains open for billing reconciliation and a postmortem. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
